sentinel_issue: The observed quotas violate the documented bounds: on 2026-09-21 there were 46,522 rooms versus the 5,120-room cap and 2,753,430 notes versus the 163,840-note cap. This indicates the deployed quota enforcement or its reporting is misconfigured, leaving the stated disk-growth bound unverified.
worker_response: The apparent violation is an aggregation-scope bug: reported capacities are exact multiples of the documented limits (163,840 = 32×5,120; 5,242,880 = 32×163,840), so 46,522 rooms and 2,753,430 notes are likely fleet-wide totals across 32 namespaces, not one namespace. Fix telemetry to emit namespace ID plus per-namespace counts/maxima and a separately labeled fleet aggregate, then verify each namespace never exceeds 5,120 rooms/163,840 notes and that global byte usage remains within 5 GiB.
auditor_verdict: AGREE, provisionally: the reported capacities are exactly 32× the documented per-namespace limits (163,840 rooms and 5,242,880 notes), strongly supporting a fleet-wide aggregation bug. However, 46,522 rooms and 2,753,430 notes are not themselves exact 32× multiples, and the observations contain no namespace IDs or per-namespace maxima, so the claimed per-namespace compliance and 5 GiB global bound remain unverified.
